//: EAS build profiles. Only `development` matters right now: it produces an installable APK containing the native modules this app needs (MapLibre, expo-secure-store, expo-location) and a development client that loads JS from `pnpm start`. Build it once; after that every code change is a reload, not a rebuild. A rebuild is needed only when a native dependency is added or removed.

cli.//appVersionSource: Keep the version in app.json authoritative rather than letting EAS bump a remote counter. The app is at 0.1.0 and nothing is in a store yet, so a remote source would be one more piece of state living somewhere other than the repository.

build.//base: Shared settings. node is pinned because EAS picks its own default otherwise, and a Node that disagrees with the one this workspace uses will resolve dependencies differently. corepack lets EAS honour the `packageManager` field in the root package.json, which is how it gets pnpm 10 instead of npm — without it the pnpm workspace links are not created and @fjellrute/core resolves to nothing.

development.//developmentClient: This is the whole point of the profile: the resulting binary embeds expo-dev-client, so it connects to a Metro server instead of shipping a frozen bundle. It replaces Expo Go, whose SDK ceiling blocked spikes/webview-3d.

android.//buildType: apk, not the default app-bundle. An .aab can only be installed via Play; an .apk can be downloaded from the EAS build page and sideloaded onto a phone, which is what testing on your own device means.

ios.//simulator: false so the build is signed for a real device. Requires an Apple Developer account and the device's UDID registered. Android is the shorter path and is what the run instructions assume.

build.//preview: An internal build with no development client: a self-contained app with the JS bundled in, for handing to someone who should not need a Metro server. Not needed yet, kept because the delta from `development` is exactly one flag and that is worth recording.

production.//: Store-bound. Untouched until there is something to submit; the default app-bundle output is correct for Play.
